model_reported.summary: Selected a bounded static row-tile variation to test indexing overhead against the measured flattened-row parent, without asserting a speedup.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique

model_reported.summary: Compared only measured aggregate outcomes as context, noted their limits, and left correctness and official one-/four-core comparison to the controller.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use as a reason to test a contrasting scheduling granularity, not as proof that row mapping caused the timing difference.
memory_lessons.claim: The explicit row-block candidate measured 0.2615 s and the flattened static-row parent measured 0.2292 s; both were correct, but the aggregate results do not isolate the cause or the one- versus four-thread behavior.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure static contiguous row tiles against the flattened row loop at the official thread settings, including full boundary and output checks.

proposal.hypothesis: The catalog contains five distinct valid OpenMP programs; the flattened static-row parent measured 0.2292 s versus the 0.4575 s serial baseline, while explicit row-block and plane-group variants were slower in aggregate. This experiment tests whether assigning static contiguous tiles of 16 rows reduces per-row y/z index reconstruction while retaining serial fallback, per-timestep regions at a one-thread budget, and a persistent team for larger budgets. The measurements must determine whether that arithmetic reduction outweighs tile-loop overhead at the official one- and four-core settings.

retained: Preserved the serial stencil implementation, output initialization, six-step parity, and low-work serial fallback.
Changed flattened row work to static tiles of 16 contiguous rows; each tile reconstructs its initial y/z position once and advances across any plane boundary.
Kept a parallel region per timestep for one-thread calls and one persistent OpenMP region across timesteps for larger budgets, using num_threads from the call and no global OpenMP state.

model_reported.summary: Compared only available aggregate measurements and explicitly left correctness checks and per-budget performance evaluation to the controller.

proposal.hypothesis: The previous development attempt failed on n=256 because its row-tile kernel covered the full x extent instead of the active interior. This candidate restricts each static z/y row to x0..x1 and tests direct collapsed row-level scheduling against the prior tiling approach. The serial cutoff remains for small workloads; one-thread calls use a region per timestep and larger budgets use one persistent team. Existing aggregate results show five distinct valid candidates, with the best at 0.2292 s versus the 0.4575 s baseline, but do not establish per-budget effects; no speedup is claimed here.

retained: Replaced tiled row worksharing with static collapsed z/y row worksharing, with each row computing only x0..x1.
Retained the serial baseline path and its low-work cutoff.
Used a separate OpenMP parallel-for region per timestep for a one-thread budget, and one persistent team with the implicit per-step worksharing barrier for larger budgets.
Preserved the six-step ping-pong order, initialization, stencil arithmetic and boundary write bounds; made no SIMD or temporal-blocking changes.
